name: Raffles Hotel Singapore
positioning: Colonial-era hotel that opened in 1887 and is a National Monument, in the heart of Singapore's business and civic district; the official site also calls it Raffles Singapore
best_for: Travelers drawn to hotel history, from the Singapore Sling to its early literary guests
Guests who want a central city base within walking distance of Esplanade - Theatres on the Bay
Travelers who value suites with butler service and garden settings

facts.text: The hotel is at the heart of Singapore's business and civic district, a preserved colonial building among modern skyscrapers.
The hotel is within walking distance of the Singapore International Convention & Exhibition Centre and Esplanade - Theatres on the Bay.
The Orchard Road shopping strip is a two-minute ride away on the Mass Rapid Transit.
The hotel opened to the public on 1 December 1887, founded by the Armenian Sarkies brothers.
Tropical gardens occupy more than a quarter of the estate.
The suites sit within colonial-style architecture with original 14ft ceilings.
The State Room Suites, in the historic Bras Basah wing, have two separate entrances, one to the parlour and one to the bedroom.
Guest amenities include personalised butler service.
Raffles Spa's hydrotherapy includes a vitality pool filled with Peruvian pink salt, a herbal sauna, an aromatherapy steam room and an ice fountain.
Butcher's Block, the wood-fire restaurant, is led by Chef de Cuisine Jordan Keao, who was born and raised in Hawaii.
Yi by Jereme Leung serves refined Chinese cuisine.
The hotel holds Three MICHELIN Keys in the MICHELIN Guide for 2026.

highlights.text: The hotel's history credits Hainanese bartender Ngiam Tong Boon with creating the Singapore Sling, so that ladies of the time could enjoy alcohol in public.
The hotel was officially declared a National Monument by the Singapore government in 1987, on its 100th anniversary.
The Palm Court Suites overlook the Palm Court, a garden reserved exclusively for hotel guests.
Early guests included the writers Joseph Conrad, Rudyard Kipling and Somerset Maugham.
The Personality Suites are a tribute to renowned past guests and feature memorabilia related to each one.

considerations.text: The setting is urban: the hotel sits in the business and civic district, surrounded by modern skyscrapers.
WhataHotel notes high tourist traffic because of the hotel's fame.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects the luxury positioning.
